Our programme includes core modules, employability events, and advanced courses to equip you with the skills and knowledge needed for managerial success in accounting and finance. Foundation year Experience a supportive university environment during your foundation year in Dubai, ensuring you’re ready to begin your undergraduate studies. When completed with at least 100 credits, you’re guaranteed progression to the BSc Business Management with Placement. You'll cover academic skills, quantitative methods for business and economics and more. Year 1 In your second year, complete 6 core modules and 4 compulsory Ministry of Education modules. Develop academic and business communication skills, master decision-making, and gain foundational knowledge in economics, accounting, and statistical analysis for a strong start to your degree. Year 2 In your third year, you'll focus on enhancing your employability with career-oriented modules and events. You can also begin to forge a global career by taking an international exchange at a number of our partner institutions across the world. Year 3 In your final year, you'll advance your knowledge with specialised courses in corporate finance, financial accounting, and management accounting. Customise your learning journey by choosing from electives such as financial statement analysis, professional development, or business analytics.

Join our three year full-time BEng programme comprising of taught and optional modules including a research project in year 3 on a topic that interests you. You'll be assessed using a combination of exams, written assignments, oral presentations, computer-based tests, laboratory and project reports, written exams and continually assessed coursework. Year 1 You'll develop the fundamental skills and knowledge needed by all engineers, while also doing aerospace-specific practicals and design work. All students take the same modules in year 1 Year 2 You'll continue to develop your engineering skills, but also study aerospace-specific topics in more depth, applying the skills you're learning. These are split between terrestrial and space areas, including aerodynamics and propulsion, aircraft design, and space systems engineering and design. You also undertake practical workshop training. All students take the same modules in year 2 Year 3 You'll learn more advanced aerospace-specific content, and apply your skills, knowledge and judgement in your individual research project (one third of this year). Both terrestrial and space content are core here, but you can focus more in these or materials for aerospace through your options. You also undertake practical flight testing, learning the skills needed to do this in reality.

You'll be equipped with a broad skillset and research experience to begin careers in in both terrestrial and space-based aerospace engineering. You could also apply your skills to pursue careers and research opportunities in non-aerospace areas where your expertise in advanced materials, manufacturing, structures, aggressive environments and remote communication and control are vitally important. To secure a place at Birmingham, you'll need to meet our general entry requirements as well as those specific to your course. A Level AAA to include A-level Mathematics and Physics or Chemistry or Further Maths or Computer Science. IB 6,6,6 at Higher Level, including Mathematics and Computer Science or Physics or Chemistry, with a minimum of 32 points overall. BTEC BTEC only considered when combined with other qualifications. We would require 2 A-levels (Mathematics and Physics) plus the BTEC. Required subjects and grades Number of A-levels required: 3. A-level Mathematics and Physics or Chemistry or Further Maths or Computer Science. General Studies not accepted. Extended Project Qualification (EPQ) Applicants who take the EPQ and meet our offer criteria will be made the typical offer for their programme of choice, plus an alternative offer which will be one grade lower plus a grade B in the EPQ. This offer would apply if you make Birmingham your firm choice. Music performance Applicants who have achieved (or who will achieve) any level 3 graded examination in music performance at grade 8 or above (e.g. ABRSM, Rockschool, Trinity College London) and outline that on their UCAS application will be made the typical offer for their programme of choice, plus an alternative offer which will be one grade lower plus the Music qualification. This alternative offer would apply if you make Birmingham your firm choice. High-level sports Applicants who play sport at county level or above will be made the typical offer for their programme of choice, plus an alternative offer which will be one grade lower. This alternative offer would apply if you make Birmingham your firm choice. If you have already received a one grade reduction through one of our performance athlete schemes (e.g. our Elite Dual Career Athlete Pathway programme), then you will not receive an additional reduction - we will apply a maximum one grade reduction on an offer. Join our four year full-time MEng programme comprising taught and optional modules. You'll be assessed using a combination of exams, written assignments, oral presentations, computer-based tests, laboratory reports and projects. Year 1 You'll develop the fundamental skills and knowledge needed by all engineers, while also doing aerospace-specific practicals and design work. All students take the same modules in year 1 Year 2 You'll continue to develop your engineering skills, but also study aerospace-specific topics in more depth, applying the skills you're learning. These are split between terrestrial and space areas, including aerodynamics and propulsion, aircraft design, and space systems engineering and design. You also undertake practical workshop training. All students take the same modules in year 2 Year 3 You'll learn more advanced aerospace-specific content, and apply your skills, knowledge and judgement in your individual research project (one third of this year). Both terrestrial and space content are core here, but you can focus more in these or materials for aerospace through your options. You also undertake practical flight testing, learning the skills needed to do this in reality. Year 4 You'll gain industry-relevant experience through a group project (50% of your final year credits, typically on either aircraft or space vehicle design), and choose options related to terrestrial and/or space applications for the other half.

You'll be equipped with a broad skillset and research experience to begin careers in in both terrestrial and space-based aerospace engineering. You could also apply your skills to pursue careers and research opportunities in non-aerospace areas where your expertise in advanced materials, manufacturing, structures, aggressive environments and remote communication and control are vitally important. Our graduates are also primed for higher research degrees in these fields. Careers Network Our aim is to make sure that success in your studies leads you on to a fulfilling career. detailSections.bodyEn: Mathematics with Business Management BSc. This undergraduate degree prepares you for high-level management positions and is an integrated programme of mathematics and business-related topics.

To secure a place at Birmingham, you'll need to meet our general entry requirements as well as those specific to your course. A Level AAA to include A-level grade A in Mathematics or Further Mathematics. IB 6,6,6 at Higher Level, including Mathematics, with a minimum of 32 points overall. BTEC only considered when combined with other qualifications. Required subjects and grades Number of A-levels required: 3, to include A-level Mathematics or Further Mathematics. A-level General Studies not accepted, but a grade A may be considered if you fail to meet your offer. Extended Project Qualification (EPQ) Applicants who take the EPQ and meet our offer criteria will be made the typical offer for their programme of choice, plus an alternative offer which will be one grade lower plus a grade B in the EPQ. This offer would apply if you make Birmingham your firm choice. Music performance Applicants who have achieved (or who will achieve) any level 3 graded examination in music performance at grade 8 or above (e.g. ABRSM, Rockschool, Trinity College London) and outline that on their UCAS application will be made the typical offer for their programme of choice, plus an alternative offer which will be one grade lower plus the Music qualification. This alternative offer would apply if you make Birmingham your firm choice. High-level sports Applicants who play sport at county level or above will be made the typical offer for their programme of choice, plus an alternative offer which will be one grade lower. This alternative offer would apply if you make Birmingham your firm choice. If you have already received a one grade reduction through one of our performance athlete schemes (e.g. our Elite Dual Career Athlete Pathway programme), then you will not receive an additional reduction - we will apply a maximum one grade reduction on an offer. Other accepted qualifications Applicants taking any additional qualifications listed below, could be eligible for an offer reduced by one grade (minimum grade A in Mathematics or Further Mathematics). STEP paper with a grade 2 Test of Mathematics for University Admissions (TMUA) with 5.0 or above Mathematics Admissions Test (MAT) with 60% or above Maths Olympiads with ‘Have participated in the International Mathematics Olympiad’ or have achieved at least a Certificate of Distinction in the British Mathematics Olympiad (Round 1 or 2) or at least a Certificate of Distinction in the UK Mathematical Olympiad for Girls Foundation Year Would you like to study this course but lack the entry qualifications? If you are not studying A-level Mathematics, you can consider a Foundation Year programme which can lead to entry onto one of our courses. Learn more: UK students (not eligible if studying A-level Mathematics) international students International entry requirements Additional requirements for select a country... English language requirements If you are an international student, you will need to demonstrate you have a suitable level of English proficiency, usually through the form of an IELTS or equivalent qualification or a Presessional English course. TOEFL tests taken before January 2026: 80 overall with no less than 19 in Reading, 19 in Listening, 21 in Speaking and 19 in Writing. TOEFL tests taken from January 2026: 4.5 Overall with no less than 4 in each skill IELTS*: 6.0 overall with no less than 5.5 in any band. Pearson Test of English (PTE): PTE 64 with no less than 59 in all four skills. Cambridge English (exams taken from 2015)***: C1 Advanced - Minimum overall score of 169, with no less than 162 in any component. Trinity ISE III: Pass in each Skill Presessional English courses If you have a conditional offer for Birmingham where English is a requirement, you can take a Presessional English course as an alternative to retaking IELTS or a similar qualifica

Join our three year full-time BSc programme comprising of taught and optional modules. You'll be assessed using a combination of exams, class tests, coursework and research projects. Year 1 You will receive a comprehensive introduction to several foundational topics in mathematics and business. All students take the same modules in Year 1 covering key topics in mathematics (foundations of calculus, linear algebra, probability) and business (marketing and finance). We place a strong emphasis on supporting the transition from mathematics at school to university. Year 2 You will build upon the foundations provided in Year 1 to obtain a more sophisticated toolkit. This will include core modules in mathematics (linear programming and complex analysis) and business (economics). You will also begin to choose optional modules in both subjects. Year 3 Building upon Years 1 and 2, you will explore advanced and specialised topics. You will explore several core modules in mathematics (game theory and integer programming) and business (supply chain management and strategic management). You will take optional modules and a project in mathematics on a topic of interest to you.

Our course offers specialised training in mathematics and business management, equipping you with the problem-solving, statistical, and strategic skills needed to thrive in various industries or pursue further academic study. Our Mathematics graduates progress into a wide range of sectors, showcasing their diverse skill set. A large proportion now work in the banking industry, as well as within sectors focusing on financial services, consulting, finance, accounting and asset management. Our graduates can be found in roles such as Director, Financial Analyst, Finance Manager, Research and Business Analyst, for companies such as Mycroft, HSBC, PwC, Golman Sachs, Intrasphere Technologies and Barclays. The University has commissioned Cturtle as our data partner for tracking our alumni destinations. The data above is a subset from 225,503 alumni who completed their studies at Birmingham up to 31 July 2025. After my second year during the summer I completed an Actuary internship with Barnett Waddingham. I found out about the opportunity by attending the Mathematics careers fair organised annually by the department, where companies both big and small who are looking to recruit University of Birmingham’s Mathematics graduates come to talk to students about the programmes they have to offer. Whilst on this internship I completed many of the jobs a trainee Actuary would do in their first year of work, gaining an insight into this type of work and developing the skills required to pursue a career in actuarial science. Completing the Mathematical Modelling and Problem Solving and Maths in Industry modules as part of my degree prepared me very well for my internship. The problem solving and teamwork skills developed in these modules helped me both when applying for this internship as I had lots of examples to draw upon at interview, as well as when completing the tasks on my internship, as I was able to approach difficult tasks and present my ideas with more confidence. As a result of this internship I have been offered a trainee Actuary role after I graduate. Immerse yourself in a course exploring the breadth and depth of chemistry alongside business management, integrating skills and careers development with core theory and hands-on lab classes. Customise your learning experience with options modules and engaging research projects to explore the frontiers of chemistry as well as its intersection with other disciplines. Year 1 All students take the same modules in year 1 to develop a comprehensive understanding of the core concepts, in inorganic, organic, physical and analytical chemistry and data analysis, that underpin more advanced study across the breadth of chemistry. Your classes will help you develop independent problem-solving and critical analysis skills, all while building your communication, presentation and team-working skills. Practical classes are carefully designed to complement the lectures and build up your skills and competencies in the lab. You'll also take business modules covering economics, finance, management and marketing taught by the experts in the School of Business here on the same campus (40 credits). Year 2 You’ll investigate broader aspects of inorganic, organic, physical and analytical chemistry, encountering topics of significance to professional chemists and exploring how these areas overlap and extend into other disciplines. Research-linked experiments further develop your skills in experimental design and the interpretation of laboratory results. You'll further your understanding of business management with modules in economics and either human resource management or marketing. Year 3 Shape your own distinctive degree based on your interests and career ambitions through the chemistry options modules and your research project. The options modules cover advanced topics across the breadth of our research expertise, and include computational, energy, materials, medicinal and sustainable chemistry. You’ll choose research projects from a range of lab-based to theoretical projects and that span core and multidisciplinary aspects of chemistry as well as educational and scientific outreach. Modules in corporate finance and supply chain management, and strategic and innovation management will further develop your understanding of underpinning business models.

Whether you choose to continue on a purely scientific path as a professional scientist or use your transferable business acumen in a more diverse career, you will graduate with sought-after skills to thrive in many industries. BSc Chemistry with Business Management will help you develop the transferable skills prized by employers, such as communication, problem-solving, project management and data analysis. Our Chemistry graduates progress into a wide range of sectors, demonstrating the breadth of their skill set. A large proportion now work in the biotechnology sector, as well as within sectors focusing on healthcare, banking and consulting. Our graduates can be found in roles such as Director, Researcher, Operations Manager, Teacher and Project Manager, for companies such as GSK, PwC, Severn Trent, Lloyds Banking and Intrasphere Technologies. The University has commissioned Cturtle as our data partner for tracking our alumni destinations. The data above is a subset from 225,503 alumni who completed their studies at Birmingham up to 31 July 2025. I currently work at Nature Publishing Group in London and after spending a couple of years as an associate editor at Nature Nanotechnology, I have been made chief editor of Nature Chemistry.
